description: We are a passionate team dedicated to solving NASA Space Apps Challenge problems through innovative, user-friendly, and interactive digital solutions. Our team brings together diverse skills in design, technology, problem-solving, and creative thinking to build engaging space-themed experiences.
summary: Rwaad: Solar Shield (Mission LUNA-1) is a bilingual (Arabic / English) 3D educational game designed for children ages 7–12 for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Players join a fictional lunar base crew to protect it during a solar storm modeled on a real NASA DONKI event: the X3.9 solar flare of May 10, 2024. The project addresses the challenge of understanding complex space weather by transforming real NASA DONKI data into an interactive, role-based gameplay experience featuring 3D station exploration and emergency shelter protocols. It is crucially important because it bridges the gap between complex space science and early education, fostering the next generation's interest in space exploration, critical problem-solving, and disaster preparedness through gamified learning.
details:
What it does and how it works: "Solar Shield: Mission LUNA-1" is a bilingual (Arabic / English) 3D educational game designed for children ages 7–12. Players join the crew of a fictional lunar base to protect it during a solar storm modelled on a real NASA DONKI event: the X3.9 solar flare of 10 May 2024, its linked coronal mass ejection (CME), and solar energetic particle (SEP) records. The game features a 3D third-person lunar base where players walk between five interactive stations (sensor dish, storm alarm, solar circuit puzzle, life-support valve, and radiation shelter) to operate hands-on equipment and manage emergency countdowns.

Benefits and Intended Impact: The project bridges the complex gap between space weather science and early education. Its primary impact is fostering early awareness of space weather phenomena, critical problem-solving, and disaster preparedness in an accessible, gamified format, while also featuring an optional Saudi Space Science station to highlight national achievements in space exploration.

Tools, Languages, and Technologies:

  • Frontend & UI: React 18, Vite 5, TypeScript, Tailwind/CSS, and i18next for full RTL Arabic/English localization.
  • 3D Graphics: Three.js via @react-three/fiber and @react-three/drei (utilizing procedural models with no external heavy asset files).
  • Motion Controls (Experimental): Powered by @mediapipe/tasks-vision (Pose Landmarker + Hand Landmarker) for webcam body tracking.
  • Backend & Data Integration: Node.js server integrating real-time NASA DONKI APIs with automated validation and a robust offline archive fallback.

Creativity and Design Considerations: The project uniquely balances rigorous scientific data with child-friendly game mechanics. It features a transparent difficulty-scoring heuristic mapped directly from NASA DONKI metrics to scale storm penalties dynamically. Furthermore, it prioritizes user privacy with local storage persistence (no accounts required) and includes experimental MediaPipe-based motion controls for an immersive, hands-on experience.
